findings.title: The NS5 Cartesian square contains additional points
findings.source_location: Acquired PDF p.48 equation(46), Corollary7.3; dependency Lemma7.7 to Theorem7.9 and current Lemma7.11.
findings.exact_example: X=T*Fl(1;3), barX=T*Fl(1,2;3), F1=<e1>,F2=<e1,e2>,N=E12; refinement admissible and N in coarse Springer image through kerN=<e1,e3>, but N(F2) is nonzero. Actual affine quotient also fails: C2=[[0,1,0],[0,0,1]],D2=[[1,0],[0,0],[0,0]],D1=0, choices C1=(0,1) and (1,0) have a common unstable affine-limit and only the latter admits required factorization.
findings.counterevidence: j remains closed and p proper in the example; all A-fixed points are in L; no counterexample to the conclusion of Lemma7.7, Theorem7.9 or normalized mirror duality.
findings.core_impact: Demonstrated false premise in the attracting-chain/support argument for the current NS5 construction.
findings.repair_boundary: A replacement proof of the required orbit-chain containment is needed; closedness alone does not repair the Cartesian assertion.

findings.title: Printed D5 table fails moment compatibility
findings.source_location: PDF p.31 Table1 and Example6.1; Proposition6.3 pp.32–33.
findings.exact_example: Full stable separated bow /1/2/3\1\, NS5 charges(1,1,1),D5 charges(2,1); split first D5 as1+1. Original moment equations vanish; printed target has residual(0,2)^T.
findings.counterevidence: The coherent negative signs in Example6.1 repair the elementary separated moment equations; existence of the intended geometric embedding is not disproved.
findings.core_impact: The stated general defining table is used in the proof of the core embedding before fusion and reduction.
findings.repair_boundary: Verified elementary sign repair and type corrections do not certify an all-charge corrected construction.

findings.title: Co-separated one-term fusion coefficient has the wrong range
findings.source_location: PDF p.39 Corollary6.14 equation(36); coherent elementary co-separated map Example6.1 p.31; Theorem6.13 p.38.
findings.exact_example: Allowed source point \3/2/1/, global charges zero, split3=1+2. Coherent resolved surface tangent at distinguished fixed point is a''/a' +(a'/a'')h. Negative Euler theta pulls back to theta(h). A stable T-fixed affine line connects this point to the actual coherent j-image. Printed coefficient theta(h)theta(h^2) differs, including at h=-1 where theta(h) is nonzero and theta(h^2)=0.
findings.counterevidence: General Theorem6.13 diagonal-factor form is not refuted. Common scalar cancellation can preserve normalized ratios and mirror duality.
findings.core_impact: Explicit failure of an advertised unnormalized fusion identity within its allowed scope.
findings.repair_boundary: Product through w'=1 is verified in this case; no all-charge corrected formula or false normalized mirror identity asserted.

findings.title: Normalization needs the attracting graph
findings.source_location: PDF pp.18–19 product inclusion and kernel specification; counterevidence Remark5.5 p.20, Proposition5.14 and Theorem6.13 proof.
findings.exact_example: X=T*P1, A=diagonal framing torus trivial on X, T=A×C_h, F=X. Printed product inclusion is identity so normal bundle zero and Thom line trivial; dual-kernel diagonal restriction is Theta(TX), with nontrivial degree from tangent weight h.
findings.counterevidence: The correct diagonal factor already appears in Remark5.5 and the inspected core proof calculations; this is the basis for Minor, not merely ease of repair.
findings.core_impact: Incorrect local specification for positive-dimensional fixed components.
findings.repair_boundary: Replace product inclusion by graph of attracting projection; imported existence theorems are not re-proved here.

findings.title: Full coefficient-field restriction is undefined
findings.source_location: AppendixA PDF pp.63–65; change-of-group map equation(33).
findings.exact_example: Allowed separated2=1+1 splitting maps u' to u-eta and u'' to u, killing nonzero t=u''-u'-eta. Since t is invertible in the source fraction field, a unital extension would yield1=0.
findings.counterevidence: Unlocalized restriction and compatible multiplicative systems exist; intended regular stable classes may be in this domain. No counterexample to the image conclusion or mirror theorem established.
findings.core_impact: Overbroad domain in an auxiliary localization argument.
findings.repair_boundary: Specify restriction before localization or the nonvanishing multiplicative system; no full rewritten proof of the intended image statement is certified.

per_problem.decision: Retain confirmed Major, with the existing local-construction versus main-theorem distinction.
per_problem.reasoning: The actual quotient-flag convention yields X=T*Fl(1;3) and the full refinement. N=E12, F1=<e1>, F2=<e1,e2> satisfy the full-flag cotangent conditions, and N belongs to the coarse image using ker N=<e1,e3>; the same F2 fails N(F2)=0, the defining incidence condition for L. This refutes (46). I also checked the stronger affine-quotient witness, rather than identifying the affinization with the Springer image: C2=[[0,1,0],[0,0,1]], D2=[[1,0],[0,0],[0,0]], D1=0, and C1=(0,1) or (1,0) obey the moment equations; both C1 are surjective, have a common unstable affine limit under g1=t, and only the second factors D2 as D C1. The triangle tail remains unchanged. Thus the actual left square in Corollary 7.3 also contains an extra point. Positive local D5 charges and the fixed-point hypothesis are met. Properness of p and closedness of j survive; all full-framing-torus fixed points lie in L. The source explicitly uses Corollary 7.3 in Lemma 7.7 and then in the support/diagonal proof of Theorem 7.9. Current v3 Lemma 7.11 is present and uses the lower fixed-point statement; no historical missing-proof allegation is adopted. A replacement orbit-chain argument is required, but the conclusions of Lemma 7.7, Theorem 7.9 and mirror duality are not disproved.

per_problem.decision: Retain confirmed Major for the printed defining table; retain the bounded sign repair.
per_problem.reasoning: For the full stable separated bow /1/2/3\1\ and split 2=1+1 I checked the supplied matrices against all adjacent moment equations. The original A=e1, a=e2, b=1 and Bminus with Bminus e1=-e2, Bminus e2=e3 satisfy the triangle equation; the displayed C,D tail satisfies the two-way equations. S1 follows from injectivity of A, S2 from the frame (Aa2,a,Ba); the semi-invariant frame argument also checks closed orbit and trivial stabilizer, rather than treating S1/S2 alone as global stability. Table 1 gives Bmid=[[0,0],[1,0]], A''=e1, a''=e2, b''=1 and hence residual (0,2)^t over C. The coherent negative a'' in Example 6.1 removes that residual; its accompanying A'=(A,-a), a'=-Bminus a and b'=(0,-1) repair the elementary separated equations. Proposition 6.3 explicitly relies on moment compatibility of the defining table. The intended embedding remains plausible and is not refuted; an all-charge corrected table and proof have not been certified.

per_problem.decision: Retain confirmed Major for the unnormalized coefficient in the allowed 1+2 co-separated split.
per_problem.reasoning: The source bow \3/2/1/ is an allowed point with zero global charges and a fixed BCT. The construction uses the coherent elementary co-separated map, not the erroneous general table. The resolved family has A=e1*, a=u, b=e2*, Bplus=u E12+E23 and the stated fixed tail; direct multiplication verifies the moment identities for every u. The covector frame (b0 A,b,b B)=I3 verifies S1, A is onto for S2, and the determinant frame criterion supplies global GIT stability. At u=0 the distinguished fixed point has the maximal two-crossing BCT; u=1 is the actual coherent j-image. The parameter has weight (a'/a'')h and is trivial after phi(a',a'',h)=(a,ah,h), so the stable affine line gives equality of endpoint pullbacks. Independently simplifying the deformation character with V=x+h+h^2, W=h+h^2, Z=h^2, x=(a'/a'')h gives M-N-g=h/x+x=a''/a'+(a'/a'')h; the dimensions 35-18-15=2 agree. The negative character pulls back to h, so the diagonal factor is theta(h), while the printed product is theta(h)theta(h^2). Their divisors differ; for real 0<q<1, h=-1 separates them without treating a pole as a valid value. This refutes (36) in its stated scope. The general diagonal-factor form of Theorem 6.13 and normalized ratios can survive; no false normalized mirror identity or all-charge repair is asserted.

per_problem.decision: Retain confirmed Minor for the positive-dimensional normalization specification.
per_problem.reasoning: Definition 5.7 and Proposition 5.8 explicitly permit arbitrary subtori. For T*P1 with the diagonal framing subtorus acting trivially, F=X and the printed product inclusion F x Attr(F) -> F x X is the identity, with zero normal bundle. The specified dual kernel instead restricts on the diagonal to Theta(TX); on the zero section its h-weight contributes degree one along E_h, incompatible with the trivial Thom line. The resonant union is empty in this example, and the definition does not require F to be proper. Replacing the product by the graph of the attracting projection restores the missing tangent/diagonal factor. Remark 5.5 and the inspected core Proposition 5.14/Theorem 6.13 computations already use the appropriate diagonal factor, supporting the local Minor classification.

per_problem.decision: Retain confirmed Minor for the domain of restriction after full fraction-field localization.
per_problem.reasoning: For the allowed separated split 2=1+1, equation (33) sends additive parameters u' to u-eta, u'' to u, and eta to itself. The nonzero polynomial t=u''-u'-eta maps to zero. A unital extension from the full source fraction field would make its inverse yield 1=0 in the nonzero target, so the displayed unrestricted localized restriction is undefined. Restriction before localization, or a multiplicative system whose images remain nonzero, is the appropriate domain correction. This does not show that the actual regular stable classes have forbidden poles, or refute the intended image statement or mirror theorem.

focused_independent_acceptance.scope_conclusion: All five existing findings were checked against arXiv:2308.07300v3, the full current report and their complete primary evidence records. Retain three Major and two Minor findings with their stated repair boundaries and counterevidence. The two geometric construction failures and the unnormalized coefficient failure are not promoted to counterexamples to normalized 3d mirror symmetry. Current Lemma 7.11 was checked in this version. No scientific report change is required.
